what_the_eye_sees: At 300 px, with no caption, this looks like a plain gold band with a smooth teardrop-shaped tag standing on top. A jewelled flower medallion is set into the tag: a red centre stone, eight blue marquise petals and an outer ring of small red beads. A jeweller would call it a gem rosette, a compass rose or a flower plaque on a signet or keyring tab. It might be called 'a round window' as a guess, but nothing says Gothic cathedral. The eight spokes are hairline and disappear at 300 px. There are no dark openings between the bars, so it doesn't read as a pierced window, and there is no tracery: no cusps, no pointed heads and no moulded frame. The stones read as flower petals laid on a solid disc, not as glass between stone bars. The frame is a bare, smooth pointed tab with flat flanks, and the band is plain from end to end, so the rest of the ring says nothing about a cathedral.
changes: Make the tracery itself the subject. Raise the 8 spokes into real bars running from the hub to the rim: about 0.9 mm wide and at least 0.6 mm proud, so they read as dark-edged gold lines at 300 px. Then sink or pierce every light between two bars by at least 0.8 mm, so each light reads as a dark cell. Finish each light's outer end in a pointed or trefoil-cusped head at the rim, so the eye sees a wheel window of lancet lights, not a flower. Acceptance: in face-300 the 8 bars and 8 dark pointed lights can be counted, and the disc no longer reads as a flat plate.

Put the stones in the lights as glass, not as petals. Seat one blue (or alternating blue and red) stone low inside each pierced light, bounded by bars on both sides. Remove the outer ring of 12 red beads, or turn them into the cusps or foils of an outer row of small round lights cut into the rim. Acceptance: the coloured stones read as filled window cells divided by gold bars; no ring of loose beads or daisy petals remains.

Turn the smooth teardrop tab into a moulded window surround and tie it to the band. Give the oculus 2 to 3 stepped concentric orders, each 0.5 to 0.8 mm, around the disc. Shape the tab's top into a crisp pointed-arch hood moulding with a ridged edge. Carry a small lancet arcade or buttress ribs down both shoulders across about 40 degrees on each side of the head, so the head no longer looks like a flat tag stuck on a plain band. Acceptance: in hero-300 the head reads as a carved window set in masonry, and the shoulders visibly carry Gothic arch work.
